Comment REWIRE & I’ll DM you a link to the full episode. 
SHARED EXPERIENCES, FALLING IN LOVE & THE ROLE OF TECHNOLOGY •
-
My guest on the Huberman Lab podcast out now is “Dr K” Dr Alok Kanojia MD @healthygamer_gg - a medical doctor (western trained and practicing MD; psychiatrist) who is also deeply trained in eastern practices.

He explains that romantic love is not dying… but it is harder to access, in part because people’s online behavior and text communications can disrupt some of the same neural pathways that romantic love and attachment require to form and be maintained. 

The episode covers a lot of topics, including navigating relationships in the larger context of the Internet and social media, specific practices to unlearn unhealthy thoughts and behaviors, and learning to identify the root causes of procrastination and how to overcome them.

On the podcast, Dr. K makes the  suggestion that people do their best to stay off their phone in the hour before dates both with new people or with your existing partner; and how the presence of the phone when you’re with someone on a date or even just with a friend or family can impede the deepening of that bond; we discussed this in the context of dopamine, signaling and more.

What’s great about Dr. K is his advice is very practical, and grounded in the neuroscience and psychiatry literature. We discussed the findings that are relevant. He’s also a clinician who sees patients and he draws from that experience as well.

You can find the episode by going to hubermanlab.com
It’s timestamp there so you can navigate quickly to the topics most of interest to you. We always include links to the various references discussed in the context of scientific findings (at the same URL).

Meanwhile, please put any questions you have in the comments section below this post (those questions could be about anything but might help me respond more quickly if they’re about brain rewiring as that’s a favorite topic and research focus of mine for many decades now).

Thank you for your interest in science! 

@stanford @stanford.med 
#neuroscience #science #relationships #neurociencia reallife
transcript: We know that one of the reasons that it's harder to fall in love is because the feeling of being in love, you know, that feeling of like we're just seeing someone and like you feel amazing and like just their presence makes you feel amazing, floods your brain with dopamine. So as our dopamine system gets messed up by social media, it is literally become neurochemically harder to fall in love. So now when I have patients, I tell them, go for a walk for one hour before you go on a date and stay off of any technology. Literally your neuroscientific capacity to fall in love is increased.
